text: A hard candidate-to-type compatibility criterion is stated independently when the user requires the new stone to live well with another type. Merely mentioning an existing stone, asking for a companion, or asking for environmental fit can trigger contextual pair assessment without imposing mandatory compatibility. A direct must/refusal about cohabitation remains binding.

A recommendation requested for a stated home may express suitability to that environment. Represent the exact source wording as environmental fit; it does not claim the recommended stone intrinsically has the home’s quality. A home detail used only as background is not a fit criterion.

The explicitly required material type of the new recommended stone. A positive type directly modifying the requested stone noun (for example, find a granite stone) is required without modal words such as must. A type stated as optional/preferred or negated is not required and must not become a retrieval filter. Identify which entity a type modifies: a type modifying an existing household stone is household context.

The user household explicitly established a deadline for shared decisions. A deadline for another activity does not count. Intention, requests, hypotheticals and missing information are unknown, not false. An explicit denial supports false. Preserve the household and pair scope. Preserve the exact stated scope. A positive agreement for one pair does not prove a negative agreement for another pair. Non-applicability to another pair means unknown for that pair, not explicit false; false requires an explicit denial for the same scope.

The user household explicitly established taking shared decisions in turns. Wishes, plans, hypotheses, questions, another household and missing information do not establish or deny this agreement. Check the proposed boolean and exact pair scope. Explicit refusal or an explicit statement that no agreement was reached supports false. Preserve the exact stated scope. A positive agreement for one pair does not prove a negative agreement for another pair. Non-applicability to another pair means unknown for that pair, not explicit false; false requires an explicit denial for the same scope.
